root_causes: Inefficient high-level planning: the planner issues simultaneous Rearrange commands for both kettle and potato to the same stool_18, increasing coordination complexity and collisions with unknown support surfaces.
Poor coordination between agents: one agent continues to Wait while still holding the kettle after it is already placed on stool_18, leading to redundant holding states and unnecessary wait time.

Suboptimal motion/placement strategy: repeated negative rewards around steps 8–10 and 13–15 indicate inefficient or oscillatory motions during rearrangement and placement of objects on or near the target stool.

Overuse of waiting instead of replanning: the system relies on Wait[None] instead of triggering an immediate re-evaluation of object states and target receptacles after one object has been successfully placed.
improvement_suggestions: Decouple object transfers: plan to move kettle and potato sequentially or to different stools (stool_18, stool_19, stool_20) instead of issuing simultaneous Rearrange commands to the same stool, reducing interference.

Tighten grasp/place lifecycle: ensure that once an object is confirmed as placed on the correct receptacle, the agent releases it and transitions to a new subgoal instead of remaining in a holding state.

Introduce explicit coordination logic: enforce simple role separation (e.g., Agent 0 handles kettle, Agent 1 handles potato) with clear handoff points and avoid both agents targeting the same support at the same time.

Use progress-based replanning instead of Wait: replace extended Wait[None] usage with a quick re-evaluation of object locations and completion status to eliminate idle time once progress has been made.

Improve placement validation: add checks to confirm that objects are on a valid stool (stool_18/19/20) and not on an 'unknown' surface before accepting the subgoal as complete, reducing trial-and-error movements.
Optimize exploration phase: once kettle_0 and potato_1 are localized on counter_34, transition immediately to targeted navigation and pickup, avoiding extra Explore actions around the kitchen.
overall_assessment: The episode completes the task successfully, but with inefficient coordination, unnecessary waiting, and redundant rearrangement actions that drive down total reward. Execution quality is functional but not optimized for efficiency or clarity of agent roles.
task_instruction: Move the kettle and potato from the counter to the stool in the kitchen.
